title: Nonlinear-bijection extension of the sum-capture theorem
summary: Determine whether the adaptive sum-capture inequality proved for linear automorphisms extends to every fixed nonlinear bijection.

formal_statement.body: Let $N=2^n$, $9n\le q\le N/2$, $P$ be a uniformly random permutation of $\{0,1\}^n$, and $Q$ be the transcript of a probabilistic algorithm making exactly $q$ adaptive two-sided queries to $P$. For a fixed bijection $\Gamma:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$, define $\mu(Q,U,V)=|\{((x,y),u,v)\in Q\times U\times V:x\oplus u=\Gamma(y\oplus v)\}|$. Does the source Theorem 1 bound $\Pr[\exists U,V:\mu(Q,U,V)\ge q|U||V|/N+2q^2\sqrt{|U||V|}/N+3\sqrt{nq|U||V|}]\le 2/N$ hold for every fixed, not necessarily linear, $\Gamma$? Prove it or give a compatible counterexample.

scope.domain: Adaptive sum-capture bounds for random-permutation transcripts over the n-bit XOR space
assumptions: The random permutation is queried adaptively in both directions exactly q times
Gamma is a fixed bijection independent of the random permutation and the algorithm's random coins
The probability is over the random permutation and the algorithm's coins and the bound is uniform over all subsets U and V
scope.unresolved_remainder: The exact high-probability inequality is proved for linear automorphisms. Later sharpened sum-capture results still assume linear Gamma, so the extension to every fixed nonlinear bijection, or a counterexample to it, remains open.
